title.value: MasakhaPOS: Part-of-Speech Tagging for Typologically Diverse African Languages
title.justification: The paper focuses on the development of a POS tagging dataset for diverse African languages.
title.quote: In this paper, we present MasakhaPOS, the largest part-of-speech (POS) dataset for 20 typologically diverse African languages.

extractions.description: The paper presents MasakhaPOS, a part-of-speech tagging dataset for 20 diverse African languages. It addresses challenges in annotating POS using UD guidelines and conducts baseline experiments with this dataset using conditional random field models and multilingual pretrained language models. Cross-lingual transfer methods are explored to improve POS tagging performance by transferring knowledge between languages.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper's focus is on natural language processing for African languages, which doesn't directly pertain to climate or ecological sustainability.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: While great strides have been made for (major) Indo-European languages such as English, French and German, work on the African languages is quite scarce.

primary_category.justification: The primary focus of the paper is linguistic development and NLP for African languages, not directly related to any ecological or climate sustainability efforts.
primary_category.quote: Our work aims to understand linguistic characteristics of African languages, we do not see any potential harms when using our POS datasets and models to train ML models.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper does not cover any secondary themes related to climate or ecological sustainability.
secondary_categories.quote: Transfer results may not generalize to all NLP tasks We have only experimented with POS task, the best transfer language e.g for non-Bantu Niger-Congo languages i.e Wolof, may not be the same for other NLP tasks.
